subject: english-language
title: Skimming, Scanning, Reading Closely
welcome_lead: Three reading speeds for three different jobs.
meta_desc: KS3 English Language adventure on skimming, scanning and close reading.
final_note: You can now skim, scan and read closely for the right purpose.

concepts.def: Slow read for detail and meaning.
Short overview of the main points.

walkthroughs.body_html: Skim for gist (top of page → end). Scan for a specific fact (eyes hunting a date or name). Different jobs.
Close reading notices verbs, images, structure — what makes the text tick. Use it for analysis, not just gist.
To annotate: underline key words, write quick questions in margins, mark devices like S (simile) or M (metaphor).

mcqs.q: A fast read for a specific fact is.
Slow read for deep detail is.
What is the difference between semantics and pragmatics?
options: Semantics studies literal meaning of words and sentences; pragmatics studies how meaning depends on context, speaker intention and conversational implicature.
Semantics is speech and pragmatics is writing.
Semantics is grammar and pragmatics is vocabulary.
Free morphemes are nouns and bound morphemes are verbs.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between free and bound morphemes?
options: Free morphemes are nouns and bound morphemes are verbs.
Free morphemes are free to use and bound morphemes cost money to use.
Free morphemes can stand alone as words ('cat', 'happy', 'run'); bound morphemes must attach to another morpheme (prefixes, suffixes — 'un-', '-ness', '-ing').
Overextension is when children speak too loudly.
